text:
Nico Hischier is the Devils' captain and the center who makes everything around him work, and this season the scoreboard has been stingy with him. With Hischier on the ice, New Jersey has scored 7.2 fewer goals than its chances deserved. That's one of the bigger gaps among forwards, and it's why he has 18 points in 26 games instead of something closer to his usual pace.

His own shooting isn't the problem. He has 10 goals on 10.16 expected goals, the most recent a classic rebound tap-in against Columbus that Mike Fink of The Hockey News called "A classic Hischier goal." The Devils get 58% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey had him 96th percentile among forwards for driving play last season while facing the other team's best.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a signature worth watching: a fifth of his setups come from behind the net, more than double a typical forward. The assists are the part most likely to rebound. Our range has him finishing with 49 to 70 points, with New Jersey rolling right now.
